items.title: macOS 27 ships an fm command-line tool for Apple's on-device Foundation Model, with an OpenAI-compatible local server
items.summary: macOS 27 includes a built-in fm CLI that calls Apple's on-device Foundation Model on any Apple Silicon Mac: fm respond for one-shot prompts, shell piping, --schema for JSON output, saved sessions under ~/.fm/sessions, and fm serve for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on localhost. Repliers who tried it say quality is limited and sessions cap at 4,096 tokens; one notes an fm chat mode and another says the Private Cloud Compute model is usable from 27.2. Not available in mainland China.

doubt.pushback: Repliers who ran it report weak output quality and a 4,096-token session limit.

items.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy: stopping tiny gradients from rounding to zero
items.summary: Barron, Gnanapragasam, Tschannen and co-authors show that standard softmax and cross-entropy round small gradients to zero once the target probability nears 1 (the cutoff tracks mantissa bits, about 5.5 nats for bf16 and 16.6 for fp32), which can destabilize training. Their reformulated functions keep those gradients without raising precision; reported results include grokking accuracy rising from 94.3% to 100% and distillation runs no longer drifting.

items.title: Layer-wise random feature models predict which training configs will spike, in seconds on a CPU
items.summary: This paper models each layer with a simple quadratic random-feature model and shows heavy-tailed data plus noisy gradients can trigger loss spikes. The cheap simulation, about 5 seconds of CPU time per layer, flagged spike-prone hyperparameter settings that matched real runs of a 1.3B-parameter Transformer.

items.title: Microduck robot walk policies trained at home on one RTX 5090, with Hermes Agent running the training loop
items.summary: A hobbyist trains walk policies for a small Microduck robot in simulation on a single RTX 5090, with Hermes Agent queuing runs, testing each walk and publishing it to Hugging Face. The new mixed-floor walk handles 25 mm steps, slippery floors, 2x shoves and gentle hills without switching policies; the walks and a skill-tree dataset are public.
